LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging practices for a binary package. It downloads the official tModLoader release zip from GitHub (pinned with a SHA-256 checksum) and the project's LICENSE file from a specific commit. The build process creates symlinks in /usr/bin and installs the zip, helper shell scripts, and license into the target directory.  

The helper `.sh` scripts are referenced via `$startdir` but are not listed in the `source` array — they are expected to be provided alongside the PKGBUILD in the AUR repository. While this means the scripts are not checksum-verified, this is a trust/transparency concern rather than evidence of malicious injection. There is no obfuscated code, unexpected network requests, or execution of unchecked content from mutable sources. All operations are confined to the package's intended installation paths.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>Standard PKGBUILD with pinned source; no malicious behavior.</summary>

LLM auditresponse for setup.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This script performs standard post-install setup for a tModLoader installation. It checks for the existence of a user data directory and compares version files between the system-wide install (`/opt/tModLoader`) and the user directory. If an update is needed, it extracts `tml.zip` from `/opt/tModLoader` into the user's directory and sets executable permissions on `start-*.sh` scripts. The script contains no network calls, no obfuscated code, no dangerous commands (eval, curl, wget, etc.), and no attempt to access or exfiltrate sensitive data. All operations are confined to the package's own directories under `/opt` and `~/.local/share/tModLoader`. This is expected behavior for a binary package that needs to copy per-user files or update them on version changes.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard post-install setup script with no malicious behavior.</summary>
</security_assessment>
